subject: Trading
title: Overcomplicating Strategies
description: Learn Overcomplicating Strategies in one minute.

hook.text: Iron butterflies, jade lizards, broken-wing condors—options strategies can get absurdly complex. Complexity isn't edge.

buildup.text: Multi-leg strategies involve 3, 4, or more options contracts. Each leg adds commission costs and execution risk.

discovery.text: More legs mean more bid-ask spreads to cross. The entry cost alone can eat into the already-thin profit margins.

twist.text: Studies show that simple strategies (covered calls, spreads) perform as well as complex ones after transaction costs.

climax.text: The best options traders use a few well-understood strategies repeatedly. Mastery beats variety every time.

punchline.text: Simple strategies, deeply understood, consistently win.

quiz.question: Why do complex multi-leg strategies often underperform?
options: Transaction costs, bid-ask spreads, and execution risk erode thin margins
